title: Apple will require 18+ for apps that offer dating, or a romantic AI companion
friendlyTitle: Apple will require an 18+ rating for dating apps, and for romantic AI companions
summary: Apple told developers on 2 November that App Store Connect will add two age-rating questions from 16 November. One covers sharing a real-world location with another person or group. The other, Dating and Relationships, covers dating between real people, or a virtual companion that engages a user in sexual or romantic content. Apps that declare the second get a minimum rating of 18+. Developers must answer when they submit an update or change the age-rating form. Every app must have the answers in by 12 January 2027. A general chatbot is not automatically covered. The companion rule is about sexual or romantic content. In Brazil, local rules set a higher bar, and an app built for family location sharing can ask the Ministry of Justice for an official rating instead.

The other covers dating between real people, or a virtual companion that engages a user in sexual or romantic content. Apps that say yes to the second question get a minimum rating of 18+. Developers must answer when they submit an update or change the age-rating form. Every app must have the answers in by 12 January 2027. A general chatbot is not automatically included. The companion rule is about sexual or romantic content. In Brazil, local rules set a higher bar, and an app built for family location sharing can ask the Ministry of Justice for an official rating instead.
whyItMatters: If a child uses an iPhone, the change is a store rating, not a new parental control you have to find. It does not start on 16 November for every app already installed. That date is when developers must start declaring the features. The deadline that covers the catalogue is 12 January 2027. If you ship an app with a companion mode, the question is whether that mode is romantic, not whether you call the app a chatbot.
